\"is_published\": true, \"raw_source_name\": \"Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems\", \"raw_type\": \"journal-article\"}, \"abstract\": \"Abstract We introduce a model for agent-environment systems where the agents are implemented via feed-forward ReLU neural networks and the environment is non-deterministic. We study the verification problem of such systems against CTL properties. We show that verifying these systems against reachability properties is undecidable. We introduce a bounded fragment of CTL, show its usefulness in identifying shallow bugs in the system, and prove that the verification problem against specifications in bounded CTL is in co NExpTime and PSpace -hard. We introduce sequential and parallel algorithms for MILP-based verification of agent-environment systems, present an implementation, and report the experimental results obtained against a variant of the VerticalCAS use-case and the frozen lake scenario.\"}, {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W7169637376\", \"doi\": null, \"title\": \"INTERPRETABLE SAFE REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR SINGLE AND MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS\", \"publication_year\": 2026, \"type\": \"dissertation\", \"cited_by_count\": 0, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"green\", \"oa_url\": \"https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/bitstreams/fc814244-694f-400b-b49e-9ca7e94e68a6/download\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"pmh:oai:wakespace.lib.wfu.edu:10339/112482\", \"doi\": null, \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/handle/10339/112482\", \"pdf_url\": \"https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/bitstreams/fc814244-694f-400b-b49e-9ca7e94e68a6/download\", \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S4377196938\", \"display_name\": \"WakeSpace Scholarship (Wake Forest University)\", \"issn_l\": null, \"issn\": null, \"is_oa\": false, \"is_in_doaj\": false, \"is_core\": false, \"listed_in\": [], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/I47251452\", \"host_organization_name\": \"Wake Forest University\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/I47251452\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [], \"type\": \"repository\"}, \"license\": null, \"license_id\": null, \"version\": \"submittedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": false, \"is_published\": false, \"raw_source_name\": null, \"raw_type\": \"Thesis\"}, \"abstract\": \"Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong potential for sequential decision-making, but its use in safety-critical domains remains limited by two persistent challenges: unsafe behavior and poor interpretability. These challenges become even more difficult in multi-agent settings, where failures can spread across interacting agents and become hard to diagnose. This thesis addresses these problems by developing interpretable methods for safety assurance in both single-agent and multi-agent RL. For single-agent RL, this thesis introduces a framework that combines local task and risk critics with a global abstract policy graph. Together, these components explain how an agent balances performance and safety, reveal adversarial vulnerabilities, support formal verification and risk-guided falsification, and enable runtime shielding without retraining. For multi-agent RL, this thesis develops gradient-based coupling analysis and a two-stage failure-forensics framework that identifies the true source of failure, distinguishes root causes from downstream effects, and traces failure propagation through interpretable contagion graphs. The proposed methods are evaluated on MuJoCo navigation tasks, a Type 1 diabetes dosing environment, Multi-Agent Particle Environments, and StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge benchmarks. The results show that these frameworks are able to explain policy behavior, uncover more safety violations than baseline verification and falsification methods, reduce unsafe behavior through shielding, and accurately identify root failure sources in multi-agent systems. Overall, this thesis shows that interpretability is not only valuable for explaining RL agents but also essential for verifying, debugging, and improving their safety in practice.\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "5ee1ae97ca3db2fd34e022cdd35a285fdaeab2ddbeb29574a5dc09e2ac7742d3", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.55277/researchhub.6q2qacii.1", "doi:10.1007/s10994-024-06543-w", "doi:10.1007/s10994-024-06543-w.pdf", "doi:10.1007/s10458-021-09529-3", "doi:10.1007/s10458-021-09529-3.pdf", "openalex:W7125432857", "openalex:W4394963598", "openalex:W3037629243", "openalex:W7169637376"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.55277/researchhub.6q2qacii.1", "https://doi.org/10.1007/s10994-024-06543-w", "https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10994-024-06543-w.pdf", "https://doi.org/10.1007/s10458-021-09529-3", "https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10458-021-09529-3.pdf", "https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/bitstreams/fc814244-694f-400b-b49e-9ca7e94e68a6/download", "https://wakespace.lib.wfu.edu/handle/10339/112482"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
